title: Eurostat euro-area HICP flash estimate (September 2026) — the first August-window-style read from outside the US
source: EST: DATE IS DERIVED, NOT SOURCED — stated plainly so nobody later reads it as confirmed. Eurostat's HICP publications page (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/hicp/publications, fetched direct 2026-09-09 by the cpi-2026-09-11 D-2 pulse-check adjacency sweep) states the cadence — 'the euro area inflation flash estimate is issued at the end of each reference month' — and its own release list gives three consecutive observed publication dates for that flash: 2026-07-01 (June data, release 2-01072026-ap), 2026-07-31 (July data, 2-31072026-ap) and 2026-09-01 (August data, 2-01092026-ap, 'Euro area annual inflation up to 3.3%'). THE AMBIGUITY IS REAL AND IS NOT SMOOTHED: those three dates show the flash landing EITHER on the last working day of the reference month (2026-07-31) OR on the first working day after it (2026-07-01, 2026-09-01), so the September 2026 flash is 2026-10-01 (a Thursday) on the two-of-three majority pattern, with 2026-09-30 (a Wednesday) the live alternative. Eurostat's own release calendar (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/news/release-calendar) was fetched direct the same day and returned only navigation chrome, no dated entries — recorded as a failed primary read, not substituted silently. Filed estimate on three separate counts, any one of which would be sufficient: the date is derived from a pattern rather than read off a schedule; this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep; and the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has IR:/BLS:/FED:/TSY:/... and no slot for a non-US statistical agency, which is the same reason the sibling entries ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and eurostat-hicp-final-2026-09-17 are filed estimate despite direct primaries. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the cpi-2026-09-11 D-2 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-09), and it exists to finish closing a coverage gap that the D-3 sweep found and only half closed. D-3 measured the gap: this calendar tracked EIGHT ECB entries and ZERO Eurostat inflation releases, which is why the euro area's August HICP flash — published 2026-09-01, and the first hard August-window inflation reading from a comparable advanced economy living through the identical energy shock — did not reach the US CPI ledger until 2026-09-08, a week late, after the D-9, D-7, D-6 and D-5 sweeps all missed it. D-3's proposal for the COMPLETE August release was promoted and is now canonical as eurostat-hicp-final-2026-09-17.json. That is the wrong half: the complete release is the confirmation two weeks later, the FLASH is the one that publishes first and the one this doc actually missed. This entry is the recurring flash, so the next US inflation sweep sees the euro-area read on its own calendar in real time instead of discovering it retrospectively. Why the shape matters and not just the level: August's flash accelerated to 3.3% almost entirely on ENERGY (14.3% y/y, from 10.3%) while SERVICES DECELERATED (3.3% -> 3.0%), which is exactly the energy-hot / core-tame shape the cpi-2026-09-11 ledger has assumed since D-25 — a cross-country corroboration no US source could supply before the US print itself. The September flash is the first euro-area reading published after BOTH ecb-decision-2026-09-10 (~99% priced for +25bp to a 2.50% deposit rate as of 2026-09-09) and fomc-2026-09-16, so it is where the two central banks' September decisions first meet fresh euro-area inflation data. Impact LOW and symbols empty, deliberately: no house playbook is rates-keyed, no tracked name carries euro-rates or euro-inflation exposure, and a flash estimate rarely moves a US tape — what the entry buys is calendar visibility, not a price channel. Read-across limit, stated so it is not overread later: euro HICP is NOT US core CPI. It carries no owners'-equivalent-rent, where US core's heaviest weight sits, and its energy weight is higher, so any comparison is DIRECTIONAL AND NEVER QUANTITATIVE. FIRST STEP FOR WHOEVER RESEARCHES THIS: verify the date against Eurostat's release calendar before anything else, because it is derived here, and amend this entry's date if the calendar says 2026-09-30. Proposed as an estimate; it widens caution and licenses nothing.
